facts.label: Verified wiring map for the UAQ install: 52-pin main harness to the big black socket; grey plug to the grey USB socket;…
facts.text: Verified wiring map for the UAQ install: 52-pin main harness to the big black socket; grey plug to the grey USB socket; bordeaux FAKRA to cellular; white FAKRA to AM/FM; mustard FAKRA to SiriusXM+GPS from the shark-fin; pink FAKRA to GPS; cream multi-pin plug and teal HSD to the back of the display. Anti-theft rule: only 3 code attempts, a third wrong entry locks the radio 30 minutes with the ignition on RUN — never guess codes on screen.

facts.label: Mounting is the remaining blocker, photo-verified Nov 14; electronics and wiring are fully proven. Display: the WK…
facts.text: Mounting is the remaining blocker, photo-verified Nov 14; electronics and wiring are fully proven. Display: the WK display's metal frame is stamped WK with about 6 tabs that do not align with the 300 bezel's 4 screw bosses, while his old display mounts by 4 corner ears on its rear metal cover; both displays have identical rear connectors (grey multi-pin + round HSD), so the fix path is swapping his old display's rear metal cover onto the WK panel. Module: the VP4 is a finned box sliding into the dash on 4 screws, while the UAQ is a flat slab with WK locating pegs and no matching screw flange — needs small L-brackets or a shop mount (DG).

facts.label: While waiting for the code, the original Harman VP4 can go back in with the same plugs (52-pin main, grey USB, four…

The two pink-looking plugs are both VP4 plugs: light pink is GPS, deeper magenta is bordeaux cellular — each only clicks into its own keyed port, never force one. Whether he completed the VP4 refit is unconfirmed; later photos show the new unit powered in the dash again at the code screen.

facts.label: The video's one-line framings, part 1: linear regression predicts a number (squared error 57% in the demo); logistic…
facts.text: The video's one-line framings, part 1: linear regression predicts a number (squared error 57% in the demo); logistic regression outputs a probability from 0 to 1; K-nearest neighbours lets 5 neighbours vote (k = 5); Naive Bayes fits one bell curve per feature; a support vector machine draws the widest street, held in place by 3 support points.

facts.label: The video's one-line framings, part 2: a decision tree asks if/else again and again (62 boxes at full depth in the…
facts.text: The video's one-line framings, part 2: a decision tree asks if/else again and again (62 boxes at full depth in the demo); a random forest lets 100 trees vote and majority wins; gradient boosting has each new tree fix what is left (882 still wrong at round 25, falling); K-means clusters with no labels needed; PCA compresses the columns.

facts.label: The video's one-line framings, part 3: a neural network bends the space and then cuts straight (67% accuracy with the…
facts.text: The video's one-line framings, part 3: a neural network bends the space and then cuts straight (67% accuracy with the best straight cut, 92% after bending); a transformer applies attention, where every token looks at every other token; diffusion turns static into a picture by denoising, step by step.

facts.label: Final leaderboard on unseen forest data: TabPFN, a transformer built for tabular data, won at 79.5%, ahead of neural…
facts.text: Final leaderboard on unseen forest data: TabPFN, a transformer built for tabular data, won at 79.5%, ahead of neural network 74.0%, random forest 73.5%, gradient boosting 72.7%, support vector machine 72.0%, K-nearest neighbours 68.3%, decision tree 64.1%, logistic regression 59.3%, and Naive Bayes last at 42.1%. K-means, PCA and diffusion were not scored; they are not classifiers here.

facts.label: The 8 architectures as function lessons: MLP = weighted sum plus a bend, stacked (depth of simple functions); CNN = one…
facts.text: The 8 architectures as function lessons: MLP = weighted sum plus a bend, stacked (depth of simple functions); CNN = one local detector reused everywhere (shared weights); RNN = state carried step to step; LSTM = gated memory, separate forget/write/reveal gates; Transformer = content-scored soft mixing (attention), powerful but O(n2) and no persistent memory; Autoencoder = bottleneck compression, keep only what rebuilds the input; GAN = maker paired with a learning critic; GNN = local message passing, global meaning emerges

facts.label: 2025-2026 status: no single architecture wins; the frontier is composition. MLP lives inside every Transformer block;…
facts.text: 2025-2026 status: no single architecture wins; the frontier is composition. MLP lives inside every Transformer block; CNN still leads edge vision; RNN/LSTM ideas revived as Mamba/RWKV/xLSTM and hybrid layers; GAN lost image generation to diffusion but survives as an adversarial critic inside other systems; GNN is the standard for relational data, with over-smoothing limits after a few hops

facts.label: Neuromorphic computing verdict: it is not a 9th architecture, it changes execution physics (spikes/events instead of…
facts.text: Neuromorphic computing verdict: it is not a 9th architecture, it changes execution physics (spikes/events instead of continuous activations, compute only on events, memory co-located with compute, local learning instead of global backprop). Honest gain is about 3x energy on matched benchmarks; 10-100x claims are vendor sparse-workload numbers. Hardware (Loihi 2, Hala Point, TrueNorth/NorthPole, SpiNNaker2) is research-lab grade; buyable chips (Akida, Pulsar) do microwatt sensor tasks only. Not needed and not available for this brain

facts.text: This brain already works neuromorphically in spirit: event-driven tunnel with zero idle sync, sparks travelling real relations, heartbeat as intrinsic rhythm, confidence gravity as a strength field, governed births as gated neurogenesis, nightly consolidation as sleep, dormant-fact pruning. Borrowable in software: spike-like pulse propagation for retrieval, STDP-analogue relation strengthening with caps/decay/audit (drift risk: feedback loops can bury rare-but-important facts), refractory/inhibition anti-noise rules, resident hot graph, delta-only ingest

facts.text: Non-registered account: An ordinary taxable investment account with no contribution limits and no special tax treatment; gains, dividends and interest are taxed yearly as earned.

facts.text: Contribution room: The amount you are allowed to put into a registered account, tracked by CRA and shown on your Notice of Assessment.

facts.label: Carry forward: Unused RRSP or FHSA contribution room that rolls into future years instead of expiring.
facts.text: Carry forward: Unused RRSP or FHSA contribution room that rolls into future years instead of expiring.

facts.label: Overcontribution: Putting more than your allowed room into a registered account, which triggers a 1% per month penalty…
facts.text: Overcontribution: Putting more than your allowed room into a registered account, which triggers a 1% per month penalty tax on the excess.

facts.label: Earned income (RRSP sense): Employment and self-employment income that creates new RRSP room at 18% of the amount, up…
facts.text: Earned income (RRSP sense): Employment and self-employment income that creates new RRSP room at 18% of the amount, up to the annual maximum.

facts.label: RRSP deduction limit: Your personal cap for deductible RRSP contributions in a year, equal to unused room carried…
facts.text: RRSP deduction limit: Your personal cap for deductible RRSP contributions in a year, equal to unused room carried forward plus 18% of the prior year's earned income, minus any pension adjustment.

facts.label: Pension adjustment: An amount reported on your T4 that reduces your RRSP room because you already earned pension…
facts.text: Pension adjustment: An amount reported on your T4 that reduces your RRSP room because you already earned pension benefits through an employer plan.

facts.label: Attribution rules: CRA rules that can tax income back in the contributor's hands when assets are gifted or loaned to a…
facts.text: Attribution rules: CRA rules that can tax income back in the contributor's hands when assets are gifted or loaned to a spouse or minor, including spousal RRSP withdrawals taken too soon.

facts.label: TFSA withdrawal and recontribution: Money taken out of a TFSA frees up that same amount of room again, but only…
facts.text: TFSA withdrawal and recontribution: Money taken out of a TFSA frees up that same amount of room again, but only starting the next calendar year, never the same year.

facts.label: HBP (Home Buyers' Plan): Lets a first-time buyer withdraw up to $35,000 from an RRSP tax free for a home purchase,…
facts.text: HBP (Home Buyers' Plan): Lets a first-time buyer withdraw up to $35,000 from an RRSP tax free for a home purchase, repaid over 15 years.

facts.label: HBP repayment: The yearly amount you must put back into your RRSP to repay an HBP withdrawal; missed repayments get…
facts.text: HBP repayment: The yearly amount you must put back into your RRSP to repay an HBP withdrawal; missed repayments get added to your taxable income.

facts.label: LLP (Lifelong Learning Plan): Lets you withdraw from an RRSP tax free to pay for your own full-time education, up to…
facts.text: LLP (Lifelong Learning Plan): Lets you withdraw from an RRSP tax free to pay for your own full-time education, up to $10,000 a year and $20,000 total, repaid over 10 years.

facts.label: First-time home buyer (FHSA meaning): For FHSA purposes, someone who did not live in a home they or their spouse owned…
facts.text: First-time home buyer (FHSA meaning): For FHSA purposes, someone who did not live in a home they or their spouse owned in the current year or the previous four years.

facts.label: CRA: The Canada Revenue Agency, the federal body that collects taxes and administers benefits, and that tracks your…
facts.text: CRA: The Canada Revenue Agency, the federal body that collects taxes and administers benefits, and that tracks your registered account room.

facts.label: T1 return: The personal income tax return every Canadian resident files each spring for the previous calendar year.
facts.text: T1 return: The personal income tax return every Canadian resident files each spring for the previous calendar year.

facts.label: Tax year: The calendar year, January 1 to December 31, that a personal tax return covers.
facts.text: Tax year: The calendar year, January 1 to December 31, that a personal tax return covers.

facts.label: Filing deadline: April 30 for most people, June 15 for the self-employed (though any balance owing is still due April…
facts.text: Filing deadline: April 30 for most people, June 15 for the self-employed (though any balance owing is still due April 30).

facts.label: T4: The slip your employer issues showing your wages and deductions for the year.
facts.text: T4: The slip your employer issues showing your wages and deductions for the year.

facts.label: T4A: A slip for other income such as self-employment payments, pensions, or scholarships.
facts.text: T4A: A slip for other income such as self-employment payments, pensions, or scholarships.

facts.label: T5: A slip reporting investment income like interest and dividends from banks and brokerages.
facts.text: T5: A slip reporting investment income like interest and dividends from banks and brokerages.

facts.label: T3: A slip reporting income from trusts and mutual funds.
facts.text: T3: A slip reporting income from trusts and mutual funds.

facts.label: NOA (Notice of Assessment): CRA's reply after processing your return, confirming your refund or balance and showing…
facts.text: NOA (Notice of Assessment): CRA's reply after processing your return, confirming your refund or balance and showing your updated RRSP and TFSA room.

facts.label: Notice of reassessment: A revised NOA CRA sends when it changes your assessment after a review or audit.
facts.text: Notice of reassessment: A revised NOA CRA sends when it changes your assessment after a review or audit.

facts.label: Taxable income: Your total income minus allowed deductions; the number your tax is actually calculated on.
facts.text: Taxable income: Your total income minus allowed deductions; the number your tax is actually calculated on.

facts.label: Net income: Total income minus certain deductions (like RRSP contributions), used to test eligibility for credits and…
facts.text: Net income: Total income minus certain deductions (like RRSP contributions), used to test eligibility for credits and benefits.

facts.label: Marginal tax rate: The tax rate on your next dollar of income, which rises as income moves into higher brackets.
facts.text: Marginal tax rate: The tax rate on your next dollar of income, which rises as income moves into higher brackets.

facts.label: Average tax rate: Total tax paid divided by total income, always lower than your marginal rate under progressive…
facts.text: Average tax rate: Total tax paid divided by total income, always lower than your marginal rate under progressive taxation.

facts.label: Tax bracket: An income range taxed at one federal (and one provincial) rate; only income inside the bracket gets that…
facts.text: Tax bracket: An income range taxed at one federal (and one provincial) rate; only income inside the bracket gets that rate.

facts.label: Basic personal amount: The slice of income every resident can earn tax free, claimed as a non-refundable credit.
facts.text: Basic personal amount: The slice of income every resident can earn tax free, claimed as a non-refundable credit.

facts.label: Deduction: An amount subtracted from income before tax is calculated, so its value equals your marginal rate (RRSP…
facts.text: Deduction: An amount subtracted from income before tax is calculated, so its value equals your marginal rate (RRSP contributions are the classic example).

facts.label: Non-refundable tax credit: A credit that reduces tax owing but can never create or increase a refund; most personal…
facts.text: Non-refundable tax credit: A credit that reduces tax owing but can never create or increase a refund; most personal credits work this way.

facts.label: Refundable tax credit: A credit paid out even when you owe no tax, effectively a benefit delivered through the tax…
facts.text: Refundable tax credit: A credit paid out even when you owe no tax, effectively a benefit delivered through the tax return.

facts.label: Capital gains: The profit when you sell an asset (stocks, property other than your principal residence) for more than…
facts.text: Capital gains: The profit when you sell an asset (stocks, property other than your principal residence) for more than you paid.

facts.label: Capital loss: The loss on such a sale, which can only offset capital gains, not other income, with unused losses…
facts.text: Capital loss: The loss on such a sale, which can only offset capital gains, not other income, with unused losses carried forward or back.

facts.label: Inclusion rate: The share of a capital gain added to taxable income; in Canada it has long been one half.
facts.text: Inclusion rate: The share of a capital gain added to taxable income; in Canada it has long been one half.

facts.label: Eligible dividend: A dividend from a large Canadian corporation, taxed more lightly because of a bigger dividend tax…
facts.text: Eligible dividend: A dividend from a large Canadian corporation, taxed more lightly because of a bigger dividend tax credit.

facts.label: Non-eligible dividend: A dividend from a small business, taxed a bit more heavily than an eligible dividend.
facts.text: Non-eligible dividend: A dividend from a small business, taxed a bit more heavily than an eligible dividend.

facts.label: Dividend tax credit: The credit that prevents double taxation of dividends by recognizing tax the corporation already…
facts.text: Dividend tax credit: The credit that prevents double taxation of dividends by recognizing tax the corporation already paid.

facts.label: Interest income: Fully taxable at your marginal rate with no special treatment, unlike gains or dividends.
facts.text: Interest income: Fully taxable at your marginal rate with no special treatment, unlike gains or dividends.

facts.label: Withholding tax (non-resident): Tax automatically held back when investment income is paid to someone outside Canada,…
facts.text: Withholding tax (non-resident): Tax automatically held back when investment income is paid to someone outside Canada, often reduced by tax treaties.

facts.label: GST: The 5% federal value-added tax charged on most goods and services across Canada.
facts.text: GST: The 5% federal value-added tax charged on most goods and services across Canada.

facts.label: HST: The harmonized sales tax used in Ontario and the Atlantic provinces, combining GST with the provincial portion…
facts.text: HST: The harmonized sales tax used in Ontario and the Atlantic provinces, combining GST with the provincial portion into one rate.

facts.label: PST (BC): British Columbia's separate 7% provincial sales tax, charged on top of the 5% GST.
facts.text: PST (BC): British Columbia's separate 7% provincial sales tax, charged on top of the 5% GST.

facts.label: CPP: The Canada Pension Plan, the mandatory earnings-based pension funded by contributions from workers and employers…
facts.text: CPP: The Canada Pension Plan, the mandatory earnings-based pension funded by contributions from workers and employers on income up to a yearly ceiling.

facts.label: CPP2 (second tier): The extra CPP layer since 2024 on earnings above the old ceiling up to a higher second ceiling,…
facts.text: CPP2 (second tier): The extra CPP layer since 2024 on earnings above the old ceiling up to a higher second ceiling, with its own contribution rate.

facts.label: OAS: Old Age Security, the monthly pension paid from general tax revenue to seniors 65 and older who meet residency…
facts.text: OAS: Old Age Security, the monthly pension paid from general tax revenue to seniors 65 and older who meet residency rules, not tied to work history.

facts.label: OAS clawback: The gradual repayment of OAS once net income passes a yearly threshold, fully eliminated at higher…
facts.text: OAS clawback: The gradual repayment of OAS once net income passes a yearly threshold, fully eliminated at higher incomes.

facts.label: GIS: The Guaranteed Income Supplement, extra monthly money for low-income OAS recipients.
facts.text: GIS: The Guaranteed Income Supplement, extra monthly money for low-income OAS recipients.

facts.label: EI: Employment Insurance, funded by payroll premiums, paying temporary income when you lose a job through no fault of…
facts.text: EI: Employment Insurance, funded by payroll premiums, paying temporary income when you lose a job through no fault of your own, plus parental and sickness benefits.

facts.label: CCB: The Canada Child Benefit, the monthly tax-free payment to families with children under 18, scaled by family income.
facts.text: CCB: The Canada Child Benefit, the monthly tax-free payment to families with children under 18, scaled by family income.

facts.label: Credit score: A three-digit number summarizing your creditworthiness, built from payment history, utilization, account…
facts.text: Credit score: A three-digit number summarizing your creditworthiness, built from payment history, utilization, account age, inquiries and mix.

facts.label: TransUnion: One of Canada's two main credit bureaus, the one Vibhu watches; lenders report your accounts here and…
facts.text: TransUnion: One of Canada's two main credit bureaus, the one Vibhu watches; lenders report your accounts here and scores are drawn from it.

facts.label: Equifax: Canada's other main credit bureau; scores can differ slightly from TransUnion because reporting is not…
facts.text: Equifax: Canada's other main credit bureau; scores can differ slightly from TransUnion because reporting is not identical.

facts.label: Credit report: Your file at a bureau listing accounts, balances, limits and payment history; free to check and worth…
facts.text: Credit report: Your file at a bureau listing accounts, balances, limits and payment history; free to check and worth reviewing for errors.

facts.label: Credit utilization: The share of your available credit currently in use; keeping each card well under 30% helps your…
facts.text: Credit utilization: The share of your available credit currently in use; keeping each card well under 30% helps your score.

facts.label: Hard inquiry: A credit check tied to an application (card, loan, mortgage) that can dip your score a few points.
facts.text: Hard inquiry: A credit check tied to an application (card, loan, mortgage) that can dip your score a few points.

facts.label: Soft inquiry: A background credit check, like checking your own score, that never affects it.
facts.text: Soft inquiry: A background credit check, like checking your own score, that never affects it.

facts.label: Grace period: The interest-free window, usually around 21 days after the statement date, to pay a credit card in full…
facts.text: Grace period: The interest-free window, usually around 21 days after the statement date, to pay a credit card in full before interest starts.

facts.label: Statement balance: What the card statement says you owe; paying this in full by the due date avoids all interest on…
facts.text: Statement balance: What the card statement says you owe; paying this in full by the due date avoids all interest on purchases.

facts.label: Minimum payment: The smallest amount a card issuer accepts each month; paying only this leaves the rest accruing…
facts.text: Minimum payment: The smallest amount a card issuer accepts each month; paying only this leaves the rest accruing interest near 20%.

facts.label: APR: The annualized interest rate on borrowed money, shown on cards and loans.
facts.text: APR: The annualized interest rate on borrowed money, shown on cards and loans.

facts.label: Cash advance: Withdrawing cash on a credit card, which starts charging interest immediately with no grace period plus a…
facts.text: Cash advance: Withdrawing cash on a credit card, which starts charging interest immediately with no grace period plus a fee.

facts.label: Balance transfer: Moving debt from one card to another, often at a low promo rate for a few months, usually with a…
facts.text: Balance transfer: Moving debt from one card to another, often at a low promo rate for a few months, usually with a transfer fee.

facts.label: NSF fee: The charge when a payment bounces for insufficient funds.
facts.text: NSF fee: The charge when a payment bounces for insufficient funds.

facts.label: Overdraft: A bank feature letting your account dip below zero for a fee plus interest, cheaper than repeated NSF fees.
facts.text: Overdraft: A bank feature letting your account dip below zero for a fee plus interest, cheaper than repeated NSF fees.

facts.label: Pre-authorized debit: Permission for a company to pull payments straight from your bank account on a schedule, used for…
facts.text: Pre-authorized debit: Permission for a company to pull payments straight from your bank account on a schedule, used for bills and insurance.

facts.label: Interac e-Transfer: Canada's bank-to-bank money transfer by email or phone number, usually arriving within minutes.
facts.text: Interac e-Transfer: Canada's bank-to-bank money transfer by email or phone number, usually arriving within minutes.

facts.label: IRCC: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, the federal department that runs immigration, work and study…
facts.text: IRCC: Immigration, Refugees and Citizenship Canada, the federal department that runs immigration, work and study permits, and citizenship.

facts.label: CBSA: The Canada Border Services Agency, the officers you meet at airports and land borders who decide entry.
facts.text: CBSA: The Canada Border Services Agency, the officers you meet at airports and land borders who decide entry.

facts.label: Express Entry: The online system managing applications for the CEC, Federal Skilled Worker and Federal Skilled Trades…
facts.text: Express Entry: The online system managing applications for the CEC, Federal Skilled Worker and Federal Skilled Trades permanent residence programs.

facts.label: Express Entry profile: Your candidate record in the Express Entry pool, scored by CRS; it stays valid for 12 months and…
facts.text: Express Entry profile: Your candidate record in the Express Entry pool, scored by CRS; it stays valid for 12 months and can be rebuilt if it expires.

facts.label: CRS: The Comprehensive Ranking System, the 1200-point score ranking Express Entry candidates on age, education,…
facts.text: CRS: The Comprehensive Ranking System, the 1200-point score ranking Express Entry candidates on age, education, language, work experience and extras.

facts.label: Draw: A round where IRCC invites the top-ranked Express Entry candidates; each draw sets a cutoff score.
facts.text: Draw: A round where IRCC invites the top-ranked Express Entry candidates; each draw sets a cutoff score.

facts.label: Cutoff score: The lowest CRS score invited in a given draw; everyone above it gets an invitation.
facts.text: Cutoff score: The lowest CRS score invited in a given draw; everyone above it gets an invitation.

facts.label: Tie-breaking rule: When several candidates share the cutoff score, only those whose profiles were submitted before the…
facts.text: Tie-breaking rule: When several candidates share the cutoff score, only those whose profiles were submitted before the draw's timestamp get invited.

facts.label: ITA: An Invitation to Apply, the formal invite giving you 60 days to submit the full permanent residence application.
facts.text: ITA: An Invitation to Apply, the formal invite giving you 60 days to submit the full permanent residence application.

facts.label: eTA: The Electronic Travel Authorization, the light pre-screening visa-exempt visitors need before flying to Canada.
facts.text: eTA: The Electronic Travel Authorization, the light pre-screening visa-exempt visitors need before flying to Canada.

facts.label: CEC: The Canadian Experience Class, the Express Entry program for people with at least one year of skilled Canadian…
facts.text: CEC: The Canadian Experience Class, the Express Entry program for people with at least one year of skilled Canadian work experience in the last three years.

facts.label: FSWP: The Federal Skilled Worker Program, the Express Entry stream for skilled workers applying from outside Canada on…
facts.text: FSWP: The Federal Skilled Worker Program, the Express Entry stream for skilled workers applying from outside Canada on a 100-point eligibility grid.

facts.label: FSTP: The Federal Skilled Trades Program, the Express Entry stream for qualified tradespeople with a job offer or…
facts.text: FSTP: The Federal Skilled Trades Program, the Express Entry stream for qualified tradespeople with a job offer or certificate of qualification.

facts.label: PNP: A Provincial Nominee Program, a province's own immigration stream; a nomination adds 600 CRS points and…
facts.text: PNP: A Provincial Nominee Program, a province's own immigration stream; a nomination adds 600 CRS points and effectively guarantees an ITA.

facts.label: Base PNP vs enhanced PNP: A base nomination goes through the province's own paper process, while an enhanced nomination…
facts.text: Base PNP vs enhanced PNP: A base nomination goes through the province's own paper process, while an enhanced nomination links to your Express Entry profile for the 600-point boost.

facts.label: Nomination (600 points): The CRS bonus for a provincial nomination, large enough to lift almost any candidate above any…
facts.text: Nomination (600 points): The CRS bonus for a provincial nomination, large enough to lift almost any candidate above any draw cutoff.

facts.label: Category-based selection: Draws targeting specific occupations or attributes (healthcare, STEM, trades, French) instead…
facts.text: Category-based selection: Draws targeting specific occupations or attributes (healthcare, STEM, trades, French) instead of ranking the whole pool by CRS.

facts.label: French-language draws: Category draws for candidates with strong French scores, historically inviting at cutoffs far…
facts.text: French-language draws: Category draws for candidates with strong French scores, historically inviting at cutoffs far below general draws.

facts.label: STEM draws: Category draws for science, technology, engineering and math occupations.
facts.text: STEM draws: Category draws for science, technology, engineering and math occupations.

facts.label: Healthcare draws: Category draws for health occupations like nurses and care aides.
facts.text: Healthcare draws: Category draws for health occupations like nurses and care aides.

facts.label: Trade draws: Category draws for skilled trades such as carpenters, electricians and welders.
facts.text: Trade draws: Category draws for skilled trades such as carpenters, electricians and welders.

facts.label: NOC: The National Occupation Classification, the catalogue assigning every Canadian job a five-digit code.
facts.text: NOC: The National Occupation Classification, the catalogue assigning every Canadian job a five-digit code.

facts.label: TEER: The six-level skill scale (0 to 5) inside NOC; TEER 0 to 3 counts as skilled work for most immigration programs.
facts.text: TEER: The six-level skill scale (0 to 5) inside NOC; TEER 0 to 3 counts as skilled work for most immigration programs.

facts.label: Skilled work (immigration sense): Work in NOC TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3, the only experience that counts for CEC and most…
facts.text: Skilled work (immigration sense): Work in NOC TEER 0, 1, 2 or 3, the only experience that counts for CEC and most Express Entry points.

facts.label: LMIA: A Labour Market Impact Assessment, the employer's government permission proving no Canadian could fill the job,…
facts.text: LMIA: A Labour Market Impact Assessment, the employer's government permission proving no Canadian could fill the job, needed for many employer-specific work permits.

facts.label: Work permit: The document letting a foreign national work in Canada; it can be tied to one employer or open.
facts.text: Work permit: The document letting a foreign national work in Canada; it can be tied to one employer or open.

facts.label: Employer-specific work permit: A permit valid only for the named employer, location and job; changing jobs needs a new…
facts.text: Employer-specific work permit: A permit valid only for the named employer, location and job; changing jobs needs a new permit or LMIA.

facts.label: Open work permit: A permit letting you work for almost any employer in Canada, such as a PGWP or a spouse's open permit.
facts.text: Open work permit: A permit letting you work for almost any employer in Canada, such as a PGWP or a spouse's open permit.

facts.label: PGWP: The Post-Graduation Work Permit, the open permit for graduates of eligible Canadian programs, lasting 8 months to…
facts.text: PGWP: The Post-Graduation Work Permit, the open permit for graduates of eligible Canadian programs, lasting 8 months to 3 years based on program length.

facts.label: Maintained status: The legal state of staying in Canada under your old permit's conditions while IRCC decides your…
facts.text: Maintained status: The legal state of staying in Canada under your old permit's conditions while IRCC decides your extension application (formerly called implied status).

facts.label: Restoration of status: The 90-day window to fix things after a temporary status expires, by applying to restore it from…
facts.text: Restoration of status: The 90-day window to fix things after a temporary status expires, by applying to restore it from inside Canada.

facts.label: Flagpoling: Leaving Canada briefly (usually to the US border) and re-entering to get same-day immigration processing,…
facts.text: Flagpoling: Leaving Canada briefly (usually to the US border) and re-entering to get same-day immigration processing, now restricted for PGWPs.

facts.label: Study permit: The document letting a foreign national study at a Canadian school; it is not a visa and does not alone…
facts.text: Study permit: The document letting a foreign national study at a Canadian school; it is not a visa and does not alone allow entry.

facts.label: DLI: A Designated Learning Institution, a school approved to host international students; only DLIs make you…
facts.text: DLI: A Designated Learning Institution, a school approved to host international students; only DLIs make you PGWP-eligible.

facts.label: Off-campus work: The limited hours a full-time student at a DLI may work during the school term, with full-time work…
facts.text: Off-campus work: The limited hours a full-time student at a DLI may work during the school term, with full-time work allowed on scheduled breaks.

facts.label: PGWP eligibility (program rule): Generally requires graduating from a full-time program of at least 8 months at an…
facts.text: PGWP eligibility (program rule): Generally requires graduating from a full-time program of at least 8 months at an eligible DLI; program length sets the permit length.

facts.label: CLB: The Canadian Language Benchmark, the 12-level scale for English ability used across immigration.
facts.text: CLB: The Canadian Language Benchmark, the 12-level scale for English ability used across immigration.

facts.label: NCLC: The French equivalent of CLB, the 12-level scale for French ability.
facts.text: NCLC: The French equivalent of CLB, the 12-level scale for French ability.

facts.label: TEF Canada: The Test d'evaluation de francais, one of the two French tests IRCC accepts for immigration, scored against…
facts.text: TEF Canada: The Test d'evaluation de francais, one of the two French tests IRCC accepts for immigration, scored against NCLC levels.

facts.label: TCF Canada: The Test de connaissance du francais, the other IRCC-accepted French test for immigration.
facts.text: TCF Canada: The Test de connaissance du francais, the other IRCC-accepted French test for immigration.

facts.label: Language test validity: Immigration language results expire after two years, so the test must be fresh when you apply.
facts.text: Language test validity: Immigration language results expire after two years, so the test must be fresh when you apply.

facts.label: NCLC 7: The French level unlocking French-category draws and bonus CRS points, roughly independent use of the language…
facts.text: NCLC 7: The French level unlocking French-category draws and bonus CRS points, roughly independent use of the language in all four abilities.

facts.label: French bonus points: Up to 50 extra CRS points for strong French (NCLC 7 or higher in all four abilities), with a…
facts.text: French bonus points: Up to 50 extra CRS points for strong French (NCLC 7 or higher in all four abilities), with a smaller bonus at lower strong levels.

facts.label: ECA: An Educational Credential Assessment, the report proving a foreign degree equals a Canadian one for immigration…
facts.text: ECA: An Educational Credential Assessment, the report proving a foreign degree equals a Canadian one for immigration points.

facts.label: WES: World Education Services, the most commonly used organization for doing ECAs.
facts.text: WES: World Education Services, the most commonly used organization for doing ECAs.

facts.label: ECA validity: An ECA stays valid for immigration for five years from its issue date.
facts.text: ECA validity: An ECA stays valid for immigration for five years from its issue date.

facts.label: Proof of funds: The bank evidence that you can support yourself after landing, required for FSWP and FSTP but not for…
facts.text: Proof of funds: The bank evidence that you can support yourself after landing, required for FSWP and FSTP but not for CEC.

facts.label: Arranged employment: A valid job offer backed by an LMIA (or LMIA-exempt in specific cases) that adds CRS points.
facts.text: Arranged employment: A valid job offer backed by an LMIA (or LMIA-exempt in specific cases) that adds CRS points.

facts.label: Sibling in Canada: Fifteen CRS points if you or your spouse has a sibling who is a Canadian citizen or permanent…
facts.text: Sibling in Canada: Fifteen CRS points if you or your spouse has a sibling who is a Canadian citizen or permanent resident living in Canada.

facts.label: Medical exam: The immigration health check by an approved doctor, screening for conditions that threaten public health…
facts.text: Medical exam: The immigration health check by an approved doctor, screening for conditions that threaten public health or would strain health services.

facts.label: Panel physician: A doctor IRCC has approved to perform immigration medical exams.
facts.text: Panel physician: A doctor IRCC has approved to perform immigration medical exams.

facts.label: Police certificate: The criminal background check from every country where you lived six months or more since age 18.
facts.text: Police certificate: The criminal background check from every country where you lived six months or more since age 18.

facts.label: Biometrics: Fingerprints and a photo collected at a visa application centre, valid for ten years across applications.
facts.text: Biometrics: Fingerprints and a photo collected at a visa application centre, valid for ten years across applications.

facts.label: Criminal inadmissibility: Being barred from Canada for past offences, from DUIs to serious crimes; some cases allow…
facts.text: Criminal inadmissibility: Being barred from Canada for past offences, from DUIs to serious crimes; some cases allow rehabilitation applications.

facts.label: Medical inadmissibility: Being barred when a condition is judged a danger to public health or likely to cause excessive…
facts.text: Medical inadmissibility: Being barred when a condition is judged a danger to public health or likely to cause excessive demand on health services.

facts.label: Misrepresentation: Giving false information or hiding material facts on an immigration application, punished with a…
facts.text: Misrepresentation: Giving false information or hiding material facts on an immigration application, punished with a five-year ban from applying.

facts.label: COPR: The Confirmation of Permanent Residence, the document issued when your PR application is approved.
facts.text: COPR: The Confirmation of Permanent Residence, the document issued when your PR application is approved.

facts.label: Port of entry: The airport or border crossing where you officially enter Canada and complete landing formalities.
facts.text: Port of entry: The airport or border crossing where you officially enter Canada and complete landing formalities.

facts.label: Landing: The final step where a new permanent resident's status is activated at the port of entry or an IRCC office.
facts.text: Landing: The final step where a new permanent resident's status is activated at the port of entry or an IRCC office.

facts.label: PR card: The wallet card proving your permanent resident status for travel; it expires every five years and is renewed…
facts.text: PR card: The wallet card proving your permanent resident status for travel; it expires every five years and is renewed from inside Canada.

facts.label: Residency obligation: The rule that a permanent resident must be physically in Canada at least 730 days in every…
facts.text: Residency obligation: The rule that a permanent resident must be physically in Canada at least 730 days in every five-year period to keep the status.

facts.label: PRTD: A Permanent Resident Travel Document, the one-use paper that lets a PR without a valid card board transport back…
facts.text: PRTD: A Permanent Resident Travel Document, the one-use paper that lets a PR without a valid card board transport back to Canada.

facts.label: Citizenship eligibility: Generally requires being a permanent resident with three years of physical presence in Canada…
facts.text: Citizenship eligibility: Generally requires being a permanent resident with three years of physical presence in Canada within the last five.

facts.label: Physical presence: Actual days your body was in Canada, counted toward citizenship; some pre-PR days count as half days…
facts.text: Physical presence: Actual days your body was in Canada, counted toward citizenship; some pre-PR days count as half days up to a cap.

facts.label: Oath of citizenship: The ceremony where you swear the oath and officially become a Canadian citizen.
